the_finding: ⛔ THE PAPER'S 'CORRECTION OF THE FIELD' DID NOT SURVIVE, AND LOSING IT IS THE RESULT. For weeks the manuscript claimed at four sites that its pooled 18.2 % (95 % CI 12.9–25.0) sits 'below the ≈27 % the field routinely quotes'. No source for that quoting practice was held anywhere — not in the manuscript, its reference list or the artifact — and the two sources in the paper's OWN reference list that state a general TAF15::NR4A3 share both give about 20 %: PMC7563993 (Stacchiotti 2020, doi 10.3390/cancers12092703) 'less frequently (about 20% of cases) to the transactivation domain of TAF15', and PMC9813045 (Bangerter, doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x) 'less frequently (approximately 20%) to TAF15'. ≈20 % lies INSIDE the pooled interval. So the pooling does not correct the literature it cites; it agrees with it, and its contribution is an INTERVAL over four independent series where that literature carries a point figure, plus the location of the referral cohort's 29.2 % within it. ⭐ THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE THAT CLOSES A CLASS RATHER THAN AN INSTANCE. The retracted ≈27 % had been sitting in the guard's DECLARED_NOT_ARTIFACT_OWNED list as `source-quoted`, which is precisely why nothing read it and why it stood at four sites. Writing the replacement into the same bucket would have reproduced the defect with a better number. It went into the artifact instead, as `analyses.C_partner_prevalence.external_reported_share`, with both quotations, both DOIs and both reference numbers, and a `falls_inside_pooled_interval` DERIVED from the interval the generator has just computed. The general rule, now in the guard's own docstring: a figure is declared unowned because the artifact has no business computing it, never because nobody has yet written down where it came from — the second case is a provenance gap wearing a declaration's clothes.
